intro: Your live post, as it has been since the 19 changes went in on 1 November. Each section those changes touched was checked in Pangram by itself: 13 sections, 10 of them Human Written, and three Mostly Human Written. Six windows read AI or Human (Low), all in your post’s words, so they’re here: 4 suggestions, and 2 lines I’d keep as they are. (The seventh was the alt text of the infographic, which isn’t prose.)

suggestions.title: “Escuelita means “little school.” …”
suggestions.where: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly, P6

edits.before: That’s where the ***escuelita*** in my title comes in. Escuelita means “little school.” I’m borrowing the word from the Zapatistas in Mexico, whose *Escuelita* brought outsiders into their communities for a while to learn autonomy by living it. In the same way, people would live in the healing communities I’m proposing, to heal and to learn the relational and practical methods, so that some of them could eventually leave and set up another one somewhere else. Otherwise, we’ve built a lovely refuge for whoever got there first.
edits.after: That’s where the ***escuelita*** in my title comes in. Escuelita means “little school.” I’m borrowing the word from the Zapatistas in Mexico, whose *Escuelita* had outsiders stay with Zapatista families for a while and learn self-government by taking part in everyday life. In the same way, people would live in the healing communities I’m proposing, to heal and to learn the relational and practical methods, so that some of them could eventually leave and set up another one somewhere else. Otherwise, we’ve built a lovely refuge for whoever got there first.

suggestions.what: “brought outsiders into their communities for a while to learn autonomy by living it” becomes “had outsiders stay with Zapatista families for a while and learn self-government by taking part in everyday life”. The link on Escuelita stays.
suggestions.why: “Learn autonomy by living it” is the abstract part. Your own section on the Escuelita, further down, says what it was: “Outsiders lived with families and learned autonomy by participating in ordinary life.”
suggestions.stays: “Escuelita means “little school.”” and the rest of the paragraph word for word.
suggestions.advice_note: I’d approve: the reader learns what the Escuelita was the first time it comes up.

suggestions.title: “I was usually just a visitor’s kid …”
suggestions.where: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly, P12

edits.before: I spent much of my childhood being carried through Twin Oaks, Acorn, East Wind, Padanaram, Zendik, and many other communities. I was usually just a visitor’s kid, close enough to see how people lived but never quite part of the tribe. At the time, that meant a lot of boredom, with some adventures mixed in, but those years gave me a great sample to compare against.
edits.after: I spent much of my childhood being carried through Twin Oaks, Acorn, East Wind, Padanaram, Zendik, and many other communities. I was usually just a visitor’s kid. I could see how people lived, but I was never really part of the tribe. At the time, that meant a lot of boredom, with some adventures mixed in, but those years gave me a great sample to compare against.

suggestions.what: One sentence becomes two, and “close enough to … but never quite …” becomes “I could see … but I was never really …”.
suggestions.why: AI (High), the only High AI window in the section. “Close enough to X but never quite Y” is a balanced turn of phrase Pangram reads as a formula; said straight, it’s the same point.
suggestions.stays: The list of communities before it and the sentence after it.

suggestions.title: “… and nobody knows anybody well enough …”

edits.before: What’s starving them is anomie. We evolved to live in small groups where everybody knows everybody. In a large society, the shared norms and close ties that held those groups together fall apart, and nobody knows anybody well enough to see what they’re really like. That’s how large societies end up run by psychopaths. (Yes, I’m always going on about this.)
edits.after: What’s starving them is anomie. We evolved to live in small groups where everybody knows everybody. In a large society, the shared norms and close ties that held those groups together fall apart, and nobody knows anybody well enough to tell who can be trusted. That’s how large societies end up run by psychopaths. (Yes, I’m always going on about this.)

suggestions.what: “to see what they’re really like” becomes “to tell who can be trusted”.
suggestions.why: Human (Low), 30 words. This is the clause you approved on 1 November (C-4) as the reason large societies end up run by psychopaths; “what they’re really like” left that reason vague. Who can be trusted is what the next sentence turns on.
suggestions.stays: The rest of the sentence and of the paragraph word for word.
suggestions.advice_note: I’d approve, if that’s the reason you meant; if not, Revise.
